speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the mechanism of injury involving a jersey pull suggests a potential avulsion fracture or ligament tear. Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to move your finger's joints without significant restriction or locking?

text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. speaker: Doctor
text:
The mechanism of injury combined with your inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the finger being stuck in extension is highly suggestive of a mallet finger or an avulsion fracture at the base of the distal phalanx. Can you confirm if you have any visible bruising or deformity at the tip of the finger, and has the pain improved at all over the last two days?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand (AP and Lateral views of the ring finger)

speaker: Doctor
text:
The X-ray results showing "Normal Readings" make an avulsion fracture highly unlikely, pointing instead toward a soft tissue injury like a mallet finger. Before we finalize the diagnosis, does your finger extend actively when you try to straighten it with your other hand?
